title: ToolACE: Winning the Points of LLM Function Calling
data_curation: ToolACE's core contribution is a synthetic data pipeline that curates a pool of 26,507 APIs across 390 domains (the broadest among peers), mixing real APIs with synthesized ones. The Tool Self-Evolution Synthesis (TSS) module runs a speciation-adaptation-evolution loop: speciation builds a hierarchical API context tree by prompting a frontier-LLM agent over API-related pretraining docs (manuals, API docs, specs, guides); adaptation samples subtrees to assign distinct domains/functionality per API; evolution iteratively generates new API definitions using an API-example buffer plus diversity indicators (new functions/params, extra constraints, type mutation, changed returns), supporting nested types like lists-of-dicts. Self-Guided Dialog Generation (SDG) uses three LLM agents (user/assistant/tool) to role-play four dialog types: single, parallel, dependent function calls, and non-tool-use. Accuracy is enforced by a Dual-Layer Verification (DLV) system: a rule checker (JSON-schema conformity, name/parameter/regex format checks, dialog correctness, sample consistency) plus an LLM model checker decomposed into hallucination detection, consistency validation, and tool-response checks, all overseen by human experts. Ablation subsets span complexity (easy/medium/hard, 60k each) and diversity (6/14/30 of 30 clusters, ~30k each).
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage with LoRA; there is no multi-stage pretrain->SFT->preference->RL ordering. The only curriculum-like mechanism is a capability-aware, self-guided complication strategy: the model to be tuned acts as a complexity evaluator using its per-sample loss to bracket an appropriate difficulty range, and the user agent's prompts are dynamically adjusted so generated dialogs sit just beyond the model's current ability (medium-complexity data trains best in ablations).
method: ToolACE is an automated agentic data-generation pipeline (not a new learning algorithm) whose three modules—TSS, SDG, and DLV (see data_curation)—produce accurate, diverse, complex function-calling SFT data tailored to the target LLM's capability. SDG's complexity evaluator measures data difficulty as the model M's negative log-likelihood H_M(x,y) over response tokens; loss is shown to correlate positively with candidate-API count, used-API count, and query/API-description dissimilarity, validating it as a difficulty signal. Multi-agent generation generates each assistant action multiple times and keeps only decisions consistent across instances, plus a structured thinking process for tool-calling. Self-guided complication re-prompts the user agent to add/remove APIs or shift query-API dissimilarity to hit the target loss band. Downstream training uses LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, all modules), learning rate 1e-4, cosine schedule, warmup ratio 0.1, batch size 48, 3 epochs, on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct (and Qwen backbones). The problem solved is scarce, inaccurate, low-diversity function-calling data that limits zero-shot tool use.
eval_metrics: Primary benchmarks are BFCL-v3 (4,951 cases: 3,951 single-turn, 1,000 multi-turn) with AST, Executable, Relevance, Irrelevance, and Overall metrics, and API-Bank (314 dialogues, 753 calls) with Call, Retrieval+Call, Plan+Retrieval+Call accuracies. General capability probes include MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, and CommonSenseQA. On BFCL-v3, ToolACE-8B ranks 3rd overall at 59.13 (Non-live AST 89.27, Non-live Exec 90.07, Relevance 85.37, Irrelevance 83.81), competitive with GPT-4-turbo (59.49) and GPT-4o (59.29) and clearly above xLAM-7b-fc-r (51.01). On API-Bank it reaches Call 75.94 and Retrieval+Call 47.41, beating all open-source models and matching GPT-4-turbo (72.43/39.26). When training on matched 25k samples, ToolACE data yields 58.19 BFCL overall versus 40.51 (xLAM) and 24.90 (ToolLLM). Ablations confirm DLV, medium complexity, and high API diversity each raise accuracy, and self-evaluation (using the learner as evaluator) beats cross-model evaluators.
key_results: ToolACE-8B (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct + LoRA) ranks 3rd on BFCL-v3 with 59.13 overall (Non-live AST 89.27, Non-live Exec 90.07), competitive with GPT-4-turbo (59.49) and GPT-4o (59.29). On API-Bank it scores 75.94 (Call) and 47.41 (Retrieval+Call), matching GPT-4-turbo and beating all open-source models. With matched 25k-sample training, ToolACE data gives 58.19 BFCL overall vs 40.51 (xLAM) and 24.90 (ToolLLM).
evolution_note: ToolACE (ICLR 2025) extends the synthetic-data-for-tool-use line of ToolLLM, ToolAlpaca, Gorilla, and xLAM, which relied on public APIs with limited diversity/complexity, by adding evolutionary API synthesis, capability-aware loss-based complexity targeting (cf. MODS, Du et al. 2023), and rigorous dual-layer verification. It shows an 8B function-calling specialist can rival GPT-4, motivating later work on high-fidelity agentic training data and verification for tool-using LLMs.
